candidates.computation_change_reason: The acute dissolved chromium III limit is hardness-dependent via the stated formula; a different hardness input or formula interpretation yields a different enforceable numeric limit for acute compliance comparison.
The chronic dissolved chromium III limit is hardness-dependent; selecting acute versus chronic or computing the formula differently changes which numeric limit applies to a reported measurement.
The acute lead limit depends on both hardness and the CF3 correction factor; interpretation of CF3 or hardness changes the computed enforceable acute limit.
The chronic lead limit uses a separate CF4 factor with the same hardness-dependent structure; different interpretation of CF4 or acute versus chronic selection changes the applicable limit.
Copper acute dissolved criteria are hardness-dependent; the chosen hardness value or formula reading alters the numeric limit used for exceedance determination.
Chronic copper limits differ from acute and are hardness-dependent; which row governs a given monitoring period changes compliance outcomes.

Ambient and effluent concentration cells are blank while instream and criteria columns read 0 or 1E+100; whether blanks denote no discharge, not monitored, or missing evidence changes the established no-data state.
Blank Ca/Ce cells paired with explicit zeros in computed columns create ambiguity between documented zero effluent, conditional non-requirement, and inadequate evidence for required monitoring.

An MQL of 0.5 is listed with blank effluent and zero instream values; interpretation determines whether beryllium monitoring was required for the period and whether absence of Ce reflects no-discharge documentation or missing evidence.

Acute aquatic (19), chronic aquatic (11), and human health (11) criteria differ; blank effluent with MQL 33 affects both which limit applies and whether chlorine monitoring was required despite no reported Ce.

No MQL or effluent values are shown for radionuclides with domestic (5) and wildlife (30) criteria; interpretation affects whether radioactivity monitoring was required and how absent results are classified.

The TMDL column uniformly reads N/A across pollutants; interpretation of whether N/A means no TMDL-based limit applies versus unknown TMDL status affects whether TMDL limits enter enforceable limit selection.
